newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka state insurance firm renews Jaffna cover.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka state insurance firm renews Jaffna cover.

text.p: Sri Lanka Insurance Corp (SLIC) said on Tuesday it had reintroduced non-life cover for the northern Jaffna peninsula a year after it was captured by government troops from Tamil Tiger rebels.
Chairman Jagath Wickremasinghe told Reuters the state-owned company would offer insurance schemes on general policies up to a maximum of 10 million rupees ($170,600) per policy.
"We have now extended a limited service," he said in an interview. "I gave instructions two weeks ago to the regional manager to resume. So far we have had no big claims."

He said the ceiling of 10 million rupees was determined by the amount SLIC could cover without relying on foreign reinsurance. He declined to say if this ceiling would be reviewed or raised in future.

The Sri Lankan government is fighting a 13-year-old war with Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels, who demand a separate homeland for the minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
Government troops took control of the entire Jaffna peninsula in 1996.
